The Lab

Concept 2 · Direction: Performance lab

This concept sells the thing national chains can’t: measurement. It opens on the fitting proposition (‘Get measured. Then buy.’) with the session itself as a readout, then treats the Motocaddy range the way an engineer would, as one spec sheet you can scan in seconds: GPS, downhill control, remote, battery, price, stock. Clubs are shown by their real loft, shaft and flex options from the catalogue. Membership is a sum. Nothing is decorative except numbers, a trajectory line and the grid. It suits the profitable side of the business (fitting and considered purchases) and makes comparison genuinely fast.

Structural changes from the brief’s section order

Fitting moves to the hero, ahead of trolleys, because it is the concept’s organising idea. Trolleys follow immediately as a flagship spec plate (M5 GPS DHC) and the full spec table, so the trolley specialism still lands in the first two screens. The three pillar tiles are folded into the hero copy. Membership becomes a calculation plus a tier comparison table. Reviews are ‘field reports’; guides are ‘test notes’.

Imagery and photography

Crisp product cut-outs on light ‘plates’, with callout lines to features. Lifestyle photography is minimal and technical: the launch-monitor screen, hands on a grip, the fitting bay under its own lighting. Graded cool and slightly desaturated. No smiling-golfer stock imagery.

Headline copy

H1: “Get measured. Then buy.”

Sub: “Free launch‑monitor fitting at our bay in Ringwood. Then the 2026 Motocaddy range and Wilson, Srixon and Mizuno clubs, specced to your numbers.”

Section heads: “2026 Motocaddy spec sheet” · “Clubs, by the numbers” · “Membership, as a sum”

Motion

Purposeful: the trajectory line draws on load (respecting reduced motion), the live status dot pulses, and table rows highlight on hover. Filters update the table instantly.

Trade-offs

Does wellFastest comparison of any concept (the spec table is genuinely useful); makes fitting feel like a precise, valuable service; distinctive in a category full of white-and-green shops; needs little lifestyle photography.
Weaker onDark UI can feel cold to older, less technical buyers, a large share of the trolley market. Dense tables need careful mobile design. Specs like weight and range must be added as Shopify metafields for this to work fully.
Build effortMedium–high. Data-driven components (filterable spec table, spec plates) need clean metafields; dark mode needs every app widget (reviews, Klarna, Acuity) themed to match.
Photography neededLow–medium: clean cut-outs (already available) plus a few technical shots of the bay and launch monitor.
Suits bestImprovers and low handicappers, gadget-minded golfers, anyone booking a fitting; buyers comparing several trolleys side by side.

EG monogram: ‘EG’ in Plex Mono inside a square Signal outline, reading like an equipment badge (suggestion only; the mark itself isn’t being redesigned here).
